description.text: Pietro Francesco Orsini was born on 2 February 1649 in Gravina in Puglia, the eldest son of Ferdinando III Orsini, 8th Duke of Gravina, and Giovanna della Tolfa. At eighteen he renounced his inheritance to join the Dominican Order, taking the name Vincenzo Maria, and was ordained in February 1671. He lectured in philosophy at Brescia and, through family influence, was made a cardinal in 1672, later serving as bishop of Manfredonia, Cesena, and archbishop of Benevento before being elected pope in 1724.

As Pope Benedict XIII, he pursued a monastic and austere reign, abolishing the Roman lottery, building hospitals, and founding the University of Camerino. He inaugurated the Spanish Steps in 1727, intervened in the relics controversy of Augustine of Hippo, and maintained a close friendship with the mystic Serafina of God. His papacy was marked by reliance on the unscrupulous secretary Cardinal Niccolò Coscia, whose financial abuses damaged the papal treasury.

curiosities.text: He inaugurated the famous Spanish Steps in Rome in 1727.
He founded the University of Camerino during his papacy.
He abolished the lottery in Rome and the Papal States, ending a practice that had benefited neighboring states.
He built several hospitals to serve the sick and poor in Rome.
He was a close friend of the mystic Serafina of God.
He was the third and last member of the Orsini family to become pope.
